title: Properties of Triangles and Quadrilaterals
seo_title: Grade 4 Triangles and Quadrilaterals Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Draw and state the properties of triangles and quadrilaterals; classify triangles and quadrilaterals according to sides and angles; differentiate different quadrilaterals.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 worksheets on triangles and quadrilaterals for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: classify triangles by sides and angles and tell squares, rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms and trapezoids apart. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Classify triangles by sides and by angles.
key_sub: A square is a rectangle and a rhombus.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Triangles by sides: equilateral (3 equal sides), isosceles (2 equal sides), scalene (no equal sides).
  • Triangles by angles: right (one 90° angle), acute (all angles less than 90°), obtuse (one angle more than 90°).
  • Quadrilaterals have 4 sides. A parallelogram has 2 pairs of parallel sides; a trapezoid has exactly 1 pair.
  • A rectangle has 4 right angles, a rhombus has 4 equal sides, and a square has both.

Examples

Example

Sides 5 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm

Two sides are equal

Answer: Isosceles triangle

Example

4 equal sides, no right angles

Opposite sides are parallel

Answer: Rhombus

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
A square is not a rectangleA square has 4 right angles, so it is a special rectangle.
Mixing up isosceles and equilateralIsosceles: at least 2 equal sides. Equilateral: all 3.
Every 4-sided shape is a rectangleCheck the angles and parallel sides.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 4 ask about triangles and quadrilaterals?
faq.a: Draw and state the properties of triangles and quadrilaterals, classify triangles and quadrilaterals according to sides and angles, and differentiate different quadrilaterals.

faq.q: Can a triangle have two right angles?
What is the difference between a trapezoid and a parallelogram?
faq.a: A trapezoid has exactly one pair of parallel sides; a parallelogram has two.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: The tick marks show that all 3 sides are equal, so it is an equilateral triangle.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: The tick marks show that all 3 sides are equal, so it is an equilateral triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its type.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is an isosceles triangle.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is an isosceles triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its type.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is an isosceles triangle.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: There are no tick marks: all 3 sides are different lengths, so it is a scalene triangle.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: There are no tick marks: all 3 sides are different lengths, so it is a scalene triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its type.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: Count the sides: there are 4, because the top corner is cut off. A triangle has exactly 3 sides.

items.q: This triangle has a right angle. Which names fit it?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is right. No sides are marked equal, so it is also scalene.

items.q: Which names fit this triangle?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, and the tick marks show 2 equal sides. So it is right and isosceles.

items.q: Which is a right triangle?
items.e: Picture A has a right angle (the small square). The others have no right angle.

items.q: Which triangle is equilateral?
items.e: Picture C has the same tick mark on all 3 sides. The two isosceles triangles have only 2 equal sides, and the scalene one has none.

items.q: Which triangle is isosceles?
items.e: Picture D has exactly 2 sides with tick marks. The others have no equal sides: they are scalene.

items.q: Which triangle is scalene?
items.e: Picture B has no tick marks: all 3 sides are different lengths. The others have at least 2 equal sides.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. What type of triangle is it?
items.e: Two sides are 5 cm, so exactly 2 sides are equal. That makes it isosceles. It is not equilateral, because 8 cm is different.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 6 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm. What type of triangle is it?
items.e: All 3 sides are different lengths, so it is scalene.

items.q: How many equal sides does an isosceles triangle have?
items.e: An isosceles triangle has exactly 2 equal sides. A triangle with 3 equal sides is equilateral.

items.q: Ana says this triangle is equilateral. Is she right?
items.e: Only the 2 long sides have tick marks, so exactly 2 sides are equal. It is isosceles, not equilateral.

items.q: Can a triangle have 2 right angles?
c: Yes, if it is very big
No, the sides would not meet
items.e: If 2 angles were right angles, the 2 sides going up from them would be parallel and never meet. The shape could not close.

items.q: What is true about the angles of an equilateral triangle?
items.e: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles. Each angle is acute (60°).

sets.title: Classify triangles by sides and angles

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is a right triangle. The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. Its full name is right isosceles triangle. The other 2 angles are acute, but a triangle is named by its largest angle.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is a right triangle. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is right scalene triangle.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: One angle is wider than a right angle, so it is obtuse. The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. Its full name is obtuse isosceles triangle. Having 2 acute angles does not make it acute: look at the largest angle.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: All 3 angles are smaller than a right angle, so it is acute. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is acute scalene triangle.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: One angle is wider than a right angle, so it is obtuse. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is obtuse scalene triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its name.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: All 3 angles are smaller than a right angle, so it is acute. The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. Its full name is acute isosceles triangle. Only 2 sides have tick marks, so it is not equilateral. Standing on its point does not change its name.

items.q: What is the full name of this triangle (angles, then sides)?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is a right triangle. There are no tick marks: all 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. Its full name is right scalene triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its name.

items.q: Which names fit this triangle?
items.e: The tick marks show 3 equal sides, so it is equilateral. An isosceles triangle has at least 2 equal sides, and this one has 3, so it is isosceles too.

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 equal sides, so it is isosceles. The third side has no tick mark, so it is not equilateral. (Obtuse describes an angle, and this triangle has no obtuse angle.)

items.q: Classify this triangle by its sides.
items.e: There are no tick marks and the 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene. (Right describes an angle, and this triangle has no right angle.)

items.q: Which is a right isosceles triangle?
items.e: Triangle C has a right angle (the small square) and 2 equal sides (the tick marks). The other right triangle is scalene, and the other isosceles triangles are acute and obtuse.

items.q: Which triangle is scalene?
items.e: Triangle A has no equal sides, so it is scalene. The others have tick marks on at least 2 sides, so they are isosceles (one is also equilateral).

items.q: A triangle has angles of 100°, 40° and 40°. Classify it by its angles.
items.e: 100° is more than 90°, so it is an obtuse triangle. Every triangle has at least 2 acute angles, so name it by its largest angle.

items.q: A triangle has three 60° angles. Classify it by its angles.
items.e: 60° is less than 90°, so all 3 angles are acute: it is an acute triangle. (Equilateral is a name by sides, not by angles.)

items.q: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. Classify it by its sides.
items.e: 2 sides are 5 cm, so it has 2 equal sides. That makes it isosceles.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 4 m, 7 m and 9 m. Classify it by its sides.
items.e: All 3 sides have different lengths, so it is scalene.

items.q: Can a right triangle also be an obtuse triangle?
c: No, only 1 angle can be 90° or more
items.e: A right angle and an obtuse angle together are already more than 180°, the total of a triangle's angles. So a triangle has at most 1 angle that is 90° or more.

items.q: Can a right triangle be isosceles?
items.e: A right isosceles triangle has a right angle and 2 equal sides, like half of a square cut corner to corner.

items.q: Which triangle is scalene?
items.e: Triangle B has no equal sides, so it is scalene. The others have tick marks on at least 2 sides, so they are isosceles (one is also equilateral).

items.q: Which is a right isosceles triangle?
items.e: Triangle A has a right angle (the small square) and 2 equal sides (the tick marks). The other right triangle is scalene, and the other isosceles triangles are acute and obtuse.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides and the small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a square. Standing on a corner does not change it: it is still a square.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, and only the opposite sides are equal, so it is a rectangle.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, and there are no right angles, so it is a rhombus.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides. There are no right angles and the sides are not all equal, so it is a parallelogram.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides, so it is a trapezoid.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides, so it is a trapezoid. The right angles do not make it a rectangle: a rectangle has 4.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides that are next to each other, not opposite. It has no parallel sides, so it is a kite.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides that are next to each other, not opposite. It has no parallel sides, so it is a kite.

items.q: The arrows show parallel sides. Which shape is NOT a parallelogram?
items.e: Picture C has only 1 pair of parallel sides, so it is a trapezoid. A parallelogram has 2 pairs. Rectangles and rhombuses have 2 pairs of parallel sides, so they are special parallelograms.

items.q: Which shape has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
items.e: Picture D is a trapezoid: only its top and bottom are parallel. The parallelogram and rectangle have 2 pairs, and the kite has none.

items.q: Which shape has 4 equal sides but no right angles?
items.e: Picture A is a rhombus: all 4 sides have the same tick mark and there are no small squares. The square has right angles, and the kite and rectangle do not have 4 equal sides.

items.q: Which shape has 4 right angles but NOT 4 equal sides?
items.e: Picture B is a rectangle. The turned square has 4 right angles too, but its 4 sides are equal. The rhombus has no right angles, and the trapezoid has only 2.

items.q: Bea says every shape with 4 sides is a rectangle. Is she right?
c: No, a rectangle needs 4 right angles
items.e: This shape has 4 sides but no right angles, so it is not a rectangle. It is a trapezoid: only 1 pair of sides is parallel.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a parallelogram have?
items.e: The opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel: top and bottom, left and right. That is 2 pairs (4 is the number of sides).

items.q: Is a square also a rectangle?
c: No, its sides are all equal
items.e: A rectangle is a 4-sided shape with 4 right angles. A square has 4 right angles too, so it is a special rectangle with 4 equal sides.

items.q: What do the arrows on the top and bottom sides show?
items.e: Matching arrows show parallel sides: they go in the same direction and never meet.

items.q: What do the small lines (tick marks) on the sides show?
items.e: Sides with the same tick marks are the same length. One tick shows one pair, two ticks show another pair.

items.q: Which shape has 2 pairs of equal sides that are next to each other, and no parallel sides?
items.e: A kite has 2 pairs of equal sides next to each other. A parallelogram and a rectangle have equal sides opposite each other.

items.q: Arnel sorts shapes into “has a right angle” and “no right angle”. Which shape goes in “no right angle”?
items.e: A rhombus that is not a square has no right angles. A square and a rectangle have 4, and a right triangle has 1.

items.q: A shape has 2 pairs of parallel sides. Its opposite sides are equal, but not all 4 sides are equal, and it has no right angles. What is it?
items.e: 2 pairs of parallel sides make a parallelogram. With no right angles it is not a rectangle, and without 4 equal sides it is not a rhombus.

items.q: Which attribute do a square and a rectangle always share?
items.e: Both have 4 right angles. A square also has 4 equal sides, but most rectangles do not.

items.q: What does every square have that not every rectangle has?
items.e: Every rectangle already has 4 right angles. A square is a rectangle that also has 4 equal sides.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: All 4 corners have the right-angle mark. Every rectangle has 4 right angles, even when it is turned.

items.q: What do shape A and shape B both have?
items.e: Both shapes have the same tick mark on all 4 sides. Only the square has right angles.

items.q: What does every square have that not every rhombus has?
items.e: Every rhombus already has 4 equal sides. A square is a rhombus that also has 4 right angles.

items.q: Which attribute do a square and a rhombus always share?
items.e: Both have 4 equal sides. A square also has 4 right angles, but most rhombuses do not.

items.q: How many right angles does every rectangle have?
items.e: A rectangle is a quadrilateral with 4 right angles. That is what makes it a rectangle.

items.q: What do shape A and shape B both have?
items.e: Both shapes have right-angle marks in all 4 corners. Only the square has 4 equal sides.

items.q: Which shape has 4 right angles?
items.e: Shape A has a right-angle mark in all 4 corners. One shape has only 2 right angles, and the others have none.

items.q: What do shape A and shape B both have?
items.e: Both are quadrilaterals with 4 sides. Only the rectangle has right angles, and only the rhombus has 4 equal sides.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: There are no right-angle marks. A rhombus has 4 equal sides, but its angles are not right angles unless it is a square.

items.q: Which shape has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
items.e: Shape B has arrows on only one pair of sides. The others have arrows on 2 pairs of sides.

items.q: What does every rectangle have that not every parallelogram has?
items.e: All parallelograms have 2 pairs of parallel sides and 4 vertices. A rectangle is the kind with 4 right angles.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The marks show right angles at 2 corners only. The other 2 angles are not right angles.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: Only one corner has the right-angle mark. The other 3 angles are bigger or smaller than a right angle.

items.q: Which shape has 4 equal sides?
items.e: Shape C has the same tick mark on all 4 sides. The others have 2 pairs of equal sides, not 4 equal sides.

items.q: A closed shape has 4 straight sides, and all 4 sides are the same length. Which name must fit it?
items.e: 4 equal sides is all a rhombus needs. It is a square only if it also has 4 right angles, and we do not know that.

items.q: How many sides of a rhombus are the same length?
items.e: A rhombus is a quadrilateral with 4 equal sides.

items.q: Which attribute does every quadrilateral have?
items.e: Every quadrilateral has 4 sides. Right angles, equal sides and parallel sides belong only to some quadrilaterals.

items.q: Which shape has 4 right angles?
items.e: Shape B has a right-angle mark in all 4 corners. One shape has only 2 right angles, and the others have none.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides and the small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a square. It is also a rhombus, a rectangle and a parallelogram, but square tells the most. Turning it on a corner does not make it a different shape.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. Only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square. It is also a parallelogram, but rectangle tells more.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. It has no right angles, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. It has no right angles, so it is not a square. Standing it on a point does not change its name.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. It has no right angles (not a rectangle) and its sides are not all equal (not a rhombus).

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezoid, not a parallelogram.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. The other 2 sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezoid, not a parallelogram. It has 2 right angles, but a rectangle needs 4.

items.q: What is the best name for this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides next to each other, so it is a kite. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus, and it has no parallel sides.

items.q: Which name does NOT fit this shape?
items.e: It has 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle, a parallelogram and a quadrilateral. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a rhombus.

items.q: Which name does NOT fit this shape?
items.e: It has 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus, a parallelogram and a quadrilateral. It has no right angles, so it is not a rectangle.

items.q: Which name does NOT fit this shape?
items.e: It has 2 pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram, a quadrilateral and a polygon. It has no right angles, so it is not a rectangle.

items.q: Which names fit this shape?
items.e: 4 right angles make it a rectangle. 4 equal sides make it a rhombus. Both together make it a square, so all three names fit.

items.q: Which shape is a rhombus but not a square?
items.e: Shape D has 4 equal sides but no right angles. The two squares are rhombuses too, but they are squares, and the rectangle is not a rhombus.

items.q: Which shape is a parallelogram but not a rectangle?
items.e: Shape C has 2 pairs of parallel sides and no right angles. The rectangle and the square have 4 right angles, and the trapezoid has only 1 pair of parallel sides.

items.q: Which shape has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides?
items.e: Shape B is a trapezoid: only its top and bottom are parallel. The parallelogram and the rhombus have 2 pairs, and the kite has none.

items.q: What must every rhombus have?
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram with 4 equal sides. It does not need right angles, and it can be turned any way.

items.q: What must every rectangle have?
items.e: A rectangle is a parallelogram with 4 right angles. Its sides may all be equal: then it is a square.

items.q: A floor tile has 4 equal sides. None of its angles are right angles. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make a rhombus. With no right angles, it is not a square.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does every parallelogram have?
items.e: A parallelogram has 2 pairs of parallel sides: each side is parallel to the side across from it. (4 is the number of sides.)

items.q: Which shape is a parallelogram but not a rectangle?
items.e: Shape A has 2 pairs of parallel sides and no right angles. The rectangle and the square have 4 right angles, and the trapezoid has only 1 pair of parallel sides.
